verdict.bounded: None of this changes the shipped scheme's fitness for its stated Phase-0 claim: byte-identical replay detection. All malleable surfaces are still covered the moment any BYTE matters (manifest/events via raw hashes; final-state via its parsed value). The gaps are representational (dup-key bytes, container bytes, snapshots) and interior-linkage completeness, which matter for cross-verifier agreement and for producers with buggy chain construction, not for the non-recomputing-mutation threat model already receipted.
verdict.corroborated: FIRST live execution of the Rust run-provenance runtime in this module's audit history. The live runtime and the independent CPython re-derivation agree bit-exact on every hash: 56/56 provenance-field/pin parity checks and 32/32 interior Haber-Stornetta event hashes recomputed bit-exact from live bytes across 7 scenarios (the 3 shipped KPI constructions, a unicode+float+snapshot stressor, and the 3 legacy 2026-receipt constructions). All 11 taxonomy probes return the analytically predicted RunArchiveError variant, covering all five variants live, including the previously untested Json-vs-Contract split (shape error -> Json; duplicate-key and syntax errors in events.jsonl -> Contract via parse_json_strict).
verdict.h0a: H0a REFUTED (predicted from source, confirmed live): the strict-parse wall covers exactly 1/5 archive surfaces (events.jsonl). manifest.json is raw-byte-bound but NEVER parsed; final-state.json is value-bound under a LENIENT parser (duplicate-key and reformat bytes accepted); provenance.json container bytes are bound by nothing verify_run checks (a decoy root_hash as first key is silently shadowed by lenient last-wins); snapshot-*.json is entirely outside the verify read-set. 2/2 duplicate-key byte streams accepted live are rejected by an RFC 8785-strict parser -- a parser differential (Momot et al. 2016) between the runtime and any canonicalization-strict external auditor.
verdict.h0b: H0b REFUTED (predicted from source, confirmed live): verify_run does NOT re-verify the interior Haber-Stornetta linkage. A hand-forged archive whose 2 event_hash fields are garbage constants passes verify_run Ok when the provenance file is arithmetically consistent with the recorded bytes; the checked predicate is only event_chain_root == last RECORDED hash plus raw file hashes. The independent oracle detects the forgery (2/2 interior recomputes mismatch), i.e. Crosby-Wallach-style full-linkage verification is strictly stronger than the shipped verifier on this axis. Consistent with (and refining) the signed anchor-necessity finding that verify_run is an internal-consistency predicate, not tamper-evidence: even internal consistency of the chain SEEDS is not checked, only hash-of-bytes consistency.
verdict.h0c: H0c REFUTED, fully localized (27/27 differential checks): the signed 2026 hash-chain-oracle-parity-v1 receipt claimed its Python mirror was 'faithfully mirroring the Rust byte formats', but its G1 archives are NOT byte-reproducible by the live runtime. Root cause (single, proven by exact reconstruction): the mirror wrote JSON in Python-dict insertion order where the live runtime serializes serde_json Values through a BTreeMap, i.e. canonically key-sorted -- affecting manifest.json bytes and the payload sub-Value inside each event line, hence manifest_sha256, events_sha256 (non-empty archives) and root_hash. All value-bound quantities (every event_hash, event_chain_root, final_state_hash) match the receipt bit-exact, and re-serializing the live content in the mirror's insertion orders reproduces every one of the receipt's divergent hashes exactly. The receipt's ALGORITHMIC claims (hash-chain arithmetic, canonicalization, tamper fail-closed logic, G0 shipped-anchor parity) all survive; what falls is only the byte-format fidelity sentence and the example manifest_sha256/events_sha256/root_hash values it recorded, which this live receipt now supersedes with runtime ground truth.
